channel.title: Paperraft
channel.description: Research in efficient inference and AI agents, ranked by independent GitHub implementations instead of citations or stars. Papers above the attention threshold are deliberately excluded.

item.title: The Expressive Power of Random-Feature MPNNs Across Graph Sizes
item.description: This is a theoretical expressivity analysis of message-passing neural networks with random node features; it replaces nothing in a production stack, as it proves approximation limits and constructions rather than proposing a deployable method. It costs nothing to adopt because there is no artifact, model, or training procedure to integrate. There is nothing that can fail in production because the contribution is a population-level framework showing size-uniform universality is impossible for standard random-feature MPNNs, plus finite-color constructions for tree subgraph isomorphism and a local MST task. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Scalable Learning of Determinantal Point Processes with Kernel-Structured Interactions
item.description: The method replaces low-rank-plus-diagonal structural constraints on the DPP kernel with a full-rank nonlinear kernel approximated by latent features and random Fourier-style features, trained via a surrogate maximum-likelihood objective with stochastic optimization. Costs include the approximation error of random-feature kernel estimation, hyperparameter sensitivity of the surrogate objective, and implementation effort for a model class outside mainstream ML tooling. It can fail if random-feature rank is too low to capture the true kernel spectrum, if item sets are small enough that exact DPP inference is cheaper and more accurate, or if the downstream task does not actually benefit from learned repulsion. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Surfing the Activation Wave: Analyzing the Information and Geometry of LLM Hidden States for Speculative Decoding
item.description: The method replaces fixed, position-based heuristics for choosing which decoder layers feed the draft model in EAGLE-style speculative decoding with a data-driven selection based on matrix entropy (informativeness), CKA (diversity), and token-entropy filtering. The cost is a one-time offline analysis pass over calibration data plus added pipeline complexity; inference architecture and memory footprint are unchanged since only the layer subset used by the draft head differs. It can fail if the calibration distribution shifts, if the gains are small relative to the already-competitive default rule (which the paper itself concedes can remain competitive), or if the statistics are computed on too few or poorly filtered tokens. 2 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Low-Rank Kolmogorov-Arnold Generator Flows for Interpretable Operator Learning
item.description: KAFlow replaces the dense, resolution-quadratic pseudo-differential symbol of the Kolmogorov-Arnold neural operator with a low-rank symbol built from univariate Kolmogorov-Arnold functions, integrated with exact exponential integrators and automatically distilled into closed form. The cost is a specialized training and gauge-fixing pipeline for scientific operator learning, plus dependence on the low-separation-rank assumption and on benchmarks that are synthetic or domain-specific; it does not address general-purpose model training or inference. It can fail when the target operator lacks low separation rank, when dynamics are not well captured by the assumed generator structure, or when data do not reach the precision regime needed for the claimed coefficient recovery. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Lightweight Time-Frequency Vibration Sensing for Consumer Device Condition Monitoring
item.description: This replaces heavier end-to-end 1-D deep models (or manual feature engineering) for vibration fault diagnosis with a two-stage pipeline: CWT or Hilbert-Huang conversion of raw vibration signals into 2-D time-frequency images, followed by lightweight image classifiers (MobileNetV3-Small, ConvNeXt-Tiny, YOLOv11-cls) sized for embedded CPUs. The cost is the added CWT/HHT preprocessing step on the edge device, image-based inference that is heavier than 1-D alternatives, and a documented accuracy drop when moving from random splits to structured isolation, i.e., leakage-free evaluation. It can fail through data leakage inflating benchmark results, poor generalization across machines, loads, or sensor placements not represented in the bearing datasets, and preprocessing latency exceeding the budget of low-end consumer microcontrollers. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: RAMP: Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision for Efficient Prefill in Recurrent-Depth Language Models
item.description: RAMP replaces uniform-precision recurrent prefill with a schedule that runs early recurrent steps in low-precision weight-and-activation arithmetic and restores full precision for terminal steps, exploiting the finding that early quantization errors are attenuated by later refinement. The cost is implementation complexity in the recurrent inference loop and the need for weight-and-activation quantization kernels, with quality risk if the error-attenuation property does not hold for a given model. It can fail on non-recurrent architectures, on workloads dominated by decode rather than prefill, and beyond the 4K context lengths actually validated. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: KV-Repurpose: A Testbed for Evaluating Non-Prefix KV-Cache Reuse
item.description: Replaces exact-prefix KV-cache reuse with segment-wise reuse, allowing cached document blocks to be reused across different system prompts and conversation histories in a vLLM-based serving stack. Costs include adopting and maintaining a custom scheduling, prompt-construction, and capacity-management layer on top of vLLM, plus engineering effort to segment workloads correctly. Naive segment reuse largely preserves quality on single-document QA and summarization, but the paper reports clear degradation in cross-document reasoning, and the reported gains are demonstrated only under a specific Zipfian RAG workload, so real traffic may benefit far less. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: TPCS: A Cycle-Level Simulation Paradigm with Native Execution Semantics for RTL Modeling and Generation
item.description: TPCS replaces event-driven RTL simulation (e.g., Verilator) with a transaction-based intermediate abstraction that uses host CPU control flow to prune inactive logic while remaining translatable to synthesizable RTL. Its cost is adoption of a new modeling framework and toolchain rather than compute or memory, since simulation runs on a host CPU. It can fail if the evaluated traces do not represent the reader's designs, if automatic RTL generation misses corner cases requiring explicit event semantics, or if ecosystem immaturity limits integration with existing verification flows. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Scaling Agentic Data for Long-Horizon Terminal Intelligence
item.description: The method replaces manually authored or naively synthesized agent training environments with a fully automated engine that reconstructs environments to preserve exploration, implementation, and verification work, then progressively expands tasks into long-horizon trajectories for supervised fine-tuning. Adopting it costs the compute to run the synthesis engine, independent execution verification, and full SFT of a 27B model, which exceeds a single 24 GB GPU and a limited cloud budget. It can fail if environment reconstruction silently reintroduces shortcuts the independent-execution check misses, and the reported gains may not transfer to a smaller model that fits the reader's infrastructure. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: RoleWorld: Knowledge Transfer in World Modeling with Functional Role Abstractions
item.description: It replaces environment-specific symbolic rules or programs with reusable functional role prototypes plus environment-specific parameter estimates, keeping transition rules fixed and refining role assignments online without LLM parameter updates. Cost is a teacher-LLM extraction phase per source environment, additional actor-LLM calls for skill-guided decision making and uncertainty-driven hypothesis testing, plus the engineering burden of maintaining executable rules, role assignments, and parameter estimators. It can fail when the teacher extracts incorrect or non-transferable role abstractions, when online parameter estimation converges too slowly or wrongly, or when the target environment's dynamics do not actually share the assumed interaction structure. 1 independent implementation, 338 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.

item.title: JANUS: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models
item.description: JANUS replaces reactive trial-and-error Generate-Execute-Feedback loops in autonomous research agents with a Predict-Verify-Evolve loop in which a co-evolving world model scores, prunes, and refines candidate branches before costly executions. The cost is maintaining an evolving candidate graph, a forecasting world model, hierarchical skill stores, and their coordination protocols, which adds orchestration complexity and extra model calls per iteration. Failure modes include miscalibrated world-model forecasts pruning valuable branches early, error compounding as skills and predictions co-evolve over long horizons, and limited transferability of gains demonstrated primarily on one benchmark. 3 independent implementations, 353 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: S$^3$R: Fast and Faithful RL Rollouts via Self-Sparse Speculative Decoding
item.description: The method replaces direct sparse-attention sampling (or plain autoregressive decoding) in RLVR rollout generation with sparse-attention drafting followed by full-attention verification and exact speculative sampling, so response groups remain faithful to the dense-policy distribution. It costs a modified inference stack: shared-parameter drafting plus verification passes, retention of the complete historical KV cache for verification, and a KV-aware scheduler to avoid offloading and restoration thrashing. It can fail because the speedup depends on draft acceptance rates and aggressive sparse budgets, requires rollout-scale infrastructure and custom scheduling unavailable on a single 24 GB GPU, and the reported gains are limited to long-context mathematical RLVR on Qwen3. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: How Much Computation Does Every Forecast Need? Structured Block Skipping in Two Time-Series Foundation Models
item.description: The method replaces full-depth forward passes in pretrained time-series foundation models with statically masked Transformer blocks, where whole blocks are bypassed using masks selected on calibration windows. It costs a calibration procedure per deployment setting and carries quality risk: aggressive skipping substantially degrades Traffic and Weather, and the measured latency gain is only 11-13% at the moderate sparsity that preserves accuracy. What can fail is generalization: dataset-specific masks transfer inconsistently, per-window optimal masks differ so no static mask captures the oracle opportunity, and Chronos representations do not support reliable routing to unseen domains. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Monarch-MoE: Structured Experts for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
item.description: Monarch-MoE replaces the dense low-rank factors in multi-expert LoRA adapters with block-diagonal factors joined by a fixed permutation, so each block-pair update touches only one output block and forgetting is reduced in multimodal continual instruction tuning. The cost is a custom implementation with batched computation, fused forward operators, and a specialized backward pass, plus method-dependent trade-offs in final-task performance; parameter savings are a side benefit rather than guaranteed speedups outside the evaluated setup. It can fail if the reader's workload is not continual multimodal instruction tuning of a ~7B VLM, since gains are validated only on MLLM-DCL and UCIT with LLaVA-1.5-7B, and the fixed permutation may underperform dense factors on other task sequences. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Understanding and Mitigating Cross-Session Attacks via Persistent Artifacts in Agent Skill Composition
item.description: It replaces unguarded cross-session skill execution, in which persistent artifacts are consumed without provenance context, with a runtime layer that restores artifact provenance and adds a pre-execution advisory review while leaving the final decision to the agent. The cost is additional engineering to record and propagate artifact provenance, extra review latency and prompt/context tokens per skill invocation, and possible advisory false positives that can block or alter legitimate flows. It can fail because the final execution choice remains with the agent, roughly one in ten attacks still succeeds in the reported setting, and provenance can be incomplete across sessions, tools, or artifact types outside the evaluated benchmark. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Forgetting is Not Always Bad: A Neuro-Inspired Memory Repair Mechanism for Poisoned LLM Agents
item.description: DREAM replaces external memory-isolation or continuous online-auditing modules for defending LLM agents against memory poisoning with an agent-intrinsic, training-free three-stage pipeline (perturbation-induced reactivation, anomaly diagnosis, selective memory suppression and reinforcement). It requires no model training and fits a single-GPU or API-based stack, but adds per-step inference overhead for reactivation and diagnosis, and its cost depends on how often repair passes must run. It can fail through false positives that suppress benign memories, degraded robustness against adaptive attackers not covered in the evaluation, and the need to revalidate detection thresholds for each memory backend and task distribution. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Agent4Spec: An LLM-based Agentic System to Optimize API Specifications through Automated Validation and Market Analysis
item.description: Agent4Spec replaces manual, one-time authoring and maintenance of OpenAPI specifications with a two-pipeline multi-agent system that self-corrects syntax errors and proposes market-driven endpoint additions. It costs multiple coordinated LLM calls per specification, which is feasible on third-party APIs with no local GPU requirement, but adds orchestration complexity and per-document token spend compared with a single lint-and-review pass. It can fail when the validation loop accepts plausible but semantically wrong corrections, and the market-analysis pipeline can generate endpoint suggestions based on unreliable competitive research that engineers must still review, since roughly half of suggestions were not adopted. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Beyond the Final Embedding: Retrieving Memories from Token-Level Evidence
item.description: The method replaces single-vector query-memory similarity with sparse token-level matching over the contextual token representations already produced by the embedding model, aggregated and combined with whole-memory similarity, optionally refined by a low-rank query adapter trained while the encoder and stored representations stay fixed. The training-free variant costs only token-level index storage and per-query matching latency, but storing token representations for all memories is substantially larger than one vector per memory, and the adapter variant adds a supervised training step with labeled data. It can fail when query-token matches fire on irrelevant memories (raising false positives), when token index size or scoring latency exceeds the memory retrieval budget, and when gains on the eight reported benchmarks do not transfer to the reader's memory distribution. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: test.

item.title: PRIME: Pre-Retrieval Index Modeling Enhancement for Structured Document Retrieval-Real
item.description: PRIME replaces plain chunk-based corpus indexing with an index-side pipeline: LLM-driven semantic restructuring of documents plus deterministic metadata extraction and hierarchical section retrieval. It costs LLM calls at index time, added indexing complexity, and a quality-fidelity trade-off from restructuring, though it reduces embedding compute and vector count by large factors. It can degrade retrieval in certain corpus regimes (three qualitative failure/success regimes are reported), and its gains are neutralized when a strong reranker is used downstream. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Masked Diffusion Language Agents for Tool-Integrated Chemical Reasoning
item.description: It replaces autoregressive left-to-right generation in tool-using agents with iterative masked-diffusion denoising over interleaved reasoning and tool-call trajectories, so tool decisions are conditioned on full-trajectory bidirectional context rather than only the past. The cost is a non-standard masked-diffusion model plus a two-stage post-training pipeline (agentic supervised fine-tuning and variance-reduced preference optimization), iterative multi-step denoising at inference, and tooling for diffusion-LM serving that is far less mature than the autoregressive stack. It can fail because the reported gains hold only on the authors' chemistry benchmark under matched budgets and may not transfer to other domains, and arbitrary-order decoding offers little benefit on strictly sequential tasks while the absence of optimized KV-cache and batching support can erode the quality advantage in latency and serving complexity. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SWE-Critix: Post-Training Generalist Verifiers for Assessing Coding-Agent Trajectories
item.description: SWE-Critix replaces prompting an off-the-shelf general-purpose LLM to judge coding-agent trajectories with a dedicated 30B verifier (Qwen3-30B-A3B) post-trained via SFT plus RL to predict completion labels and produce natural-language explanations. The reader cannot reproduce the training pipeline, but the released 30B-A3B MoE model can run quantized on a 24 GB GPU or via API, at the cost of serving a large model and adding a verification step to every agent run. It can fail because 78% accuracy still means roughly one in five judgments is wrong, the verifier is trained on CodeForge-Preview trajectories and may degrade on other agents, repositories, or task distributions, and verifier errors can silently propagate if used for automated filtering or reward signals. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AgentSWE: Can Coding Agents Build the Agent You Actually Want?
item.description: AgentSWE replaces ad hoc acceptance of agent-generated agent code with commission-style evaluation: a frozen submission is tested on held-out cases graded against requirement-derived rubrics under pass/fail gates, rather than being judged by its behavior on the illustrative cases the builder saw. The cost is evaluation engineering effort: constructing held-out cases and rubrics per requirement, plus the API or GPU spend to run frozen submissions, and it measures rather than improves delivered quality. It can fail to transfer if the reader's tasks are narrower than the benchmark's 25 commissions, and rubric-based grading inherits the reliability limits of whatever grader is used. 1 independent implementation, 12 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ProgramGym: Scaling Training Environments for Long-Horizon Program Reproduction Agents
item.description: Program-Agent replaces a single monolithic coding-agent loop with a role-isolated workflow (analysis, implementation, review) plus revision management for compilation checks and failure recovery, which a small team can replicate as prompting/orchestration over API models; Program-Env replaces hand-built training environments with a feedback-driven pipeline that repairs sandbox builds and black-box tests. The agent-side cost is higher token consumption and latency from multi-role passes and exploratory analysis before implementation; the environment-side cost is substantial engineering and compute to build and verify 1,648 sandboxed repositories, which is not realistic on one 24 GB GPU. Failure modes include compounding errors across role handoffs, reference exploration that consumes context without improving the implementation, and environment/test suites whose black-box tests are too weak to verify correctness, so reproduced gains may not transfer to benchmarks other than ProgramBench. 3 independent implementations, 21 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ShoreKeeper: Accelerating Iterative Data Analytics in the Cloud via Distributed Recovery-Cost-Aware Caching
item.description: ShoreKeeper replaces node-local cache eviction policies in distributed dataflow systems with a cluster-wide optimization model that treats aggregate memory as one elastic pool and minimizes the recomputation cost of evicted intermediates, including on preemptible instances. It costs a global caching-plan solver plus graph-pruning refinement, adding control-plane complexity and dependence on accurate dataflow lineage and recovery-cost estimates. It can fail when working sets or cluster membership shift faster than the plan can be refined, when recovery costs are misestimated, or in single-node deployments where there is no distributed memory pool to coordinate. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access
item.description: Web$hell replaces separate search-augmented, browser-based, and filesystem-based web access models with a single compiled interface in which webpages are converted into addressable information and action objects maintained in a shared cache. The cost is the added compilation and caching layer (WebContract schema, WebCompiler, WebCache), which introduces engineering complexity and per-page processing overhead on top of existing LLM API calls. It can fail when the compiler loses information present in raw pages or screenshots, when cached objects go stale on dynamic sites, or when the abstraction does not cover site-specific interactions a real browser would handle. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Rollout-Time Intervention: Unlocking Agentic Reinforcement Learning Beyond Policy Limits
item.description: RTI replaces purely on-policy exploration in agentic RL by injecting reward-rubric evidence during rollout to convert failed trajectories into successful ones, then filtering interventions with excessive distributional shift before policy optimization. It costs additional rollout compute for intervention and filtering, requires well-specified evaluation rubrics per task, and adds off-policy correction logic to the training pipeline. It can fail when rubrics are unavailable or noisy, when filtering admits trajectories whose distribution shift destabilizes training, or when the resulting training still demands more GPU memory than a single 24 GB card provides for the chosen model size. 2 independent implementations, 449 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Towards Enriching Design-Time Models with Evidence from Simulation and Operational Activities
item.description: The paper proposes a model-based systems engineering (MBSE) workflow that replaces ad hoc, implicit transfer of simulation and operational observations into design-time artefacts (specifically Influence Models for cyber-physical systems) with a systematic evidence-driven procedure for participant pruning, interaction characterisation, influence-function abstraction, and validity scoping. Adoption costs are process and tooling overhead: teams must instrument simulation and operational activities, curate evidence traces, and maintain enriched design models, none of which involves GPU compute, model training, or LLM inference infrastructure. It can fail when evidence is sparse, unrepresentative of operational conditions, or when the cost of maintaining model-evidence traceability exceeds the reasoning benefit in subsequent design iterations. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: CompileMask: Bridging the Gap Between Expressiveness and Efficiency in Attention Masking
item.description: It replaces predicate-based custom masking, which materializes or evaluates masks expensively, and fixed-count interval masking, which limits expressiveness, with an offline-compiled MaskSpec rule that emits a preprocess kernel and a compact Execution Descriptor for endpoint comparisons. The cost is an added compiler and DSL dependency, integration with a compatible attention kernel, an online preprocessing step that reads batch metadata, and engineering effort that is only justified when runtime-dependent masks are a measured bottleneck. It can fail when visibility rules are not reducible to region endpoints, when metadata changes in ways the descriptor cannot represent, when the target attention backend is unsupported, or when the workload uses standard causal or full masks and sees little benefit. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Proactive Agentic Orchestration
item.description: POrchestra replaces static multi-agent orchestration, in which sub-agent goals and harnesses are fixed at creation, with sub-agents that can request runtime adjustments from the orchestrator; OPOD optionally replaces sparse-reward RL on the orchestration policy with process supervision distilled from hindsight revision requests. The cost is extra orchestrator-sub-agent communication rounds (added latency and tokens), plus training infrastructure for OPOD if the distillation component is adopted, though the runtime mechanism alone works with API models. It can fail when sub-agents issue unnecessary or poorly targeted revision requests, adding cost without quality gain, and the reported gains are benchmark averages that may not transfer to a different task mix or model family. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Humanize MLE Agents: Multi-Agent Session Alternation Beyond Single-Agent Limits
item.description: HMA replaces single long-horizon agent sessions with custom context-engineering harnesses by alternating two agents over a shared workspace, capping each session at k experiments and resetting context between sessions. The cost is orchestration logic and duplicated token spend across sessions (each agent re-reads workspace state), though the paper reports a 4x reduction in wall-clock budget relative to the baseline; it requires API access to two capable LLM agents, which fits constrained infrastructure. It can fail when the two agents lack complementary strengths, when workspace state summaries lose critical experiment context across resets, or when the task is short enough that single-session deceleration never materializes. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Humanize Olympiad Agents: A Multi-Session Workflow for Olympiad Problem Solving with Solve, Review, Wiki, Verify
item.description: It replaces single-session agent attempts on hard reasoning problems with a multi-session pipeline that adds an independent reviewer, a task-specific structured wiki, and a Lean-based verifier checking proofs against trusted statements. The cost is substantially higher inference spending (multiple sessions plus reviewer and verifier calls per problem), added orchestration complexity, and dependence on frontier models and a Lean formalization stack. Failure modes include reviewer errors propagating as authoritative feedback, wiki content being incomplete or wrong, verifier gaps when no formal statement exists for a task, and inference costs that scale poorly on a limited budget. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: (When) Should a Software Factory be Lights-off? Benchmarking Code Review Agents on Bug Detection
item.description: The method replaces human-first-pass code review on agent-generated pull requests with an LLM review agent, optionally steered by exploration-nudging prompts and supplied repository context. Cost is per-PR API inference (about 10% more for the improved prompting) plus pipeline work to supply project knowledge and to scale review effort with PR complexity. Detection degrades on complex changes, on bugs requiring non-local reasoning, and sharply on proprietary code where project context is missing, so fully lights-off review would silently pass bugs. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction
item.description: Replaces LLM fine-tuning for self-correction (revision/feedback training) with a 130K-parameter MLP head on a frozen encoder that selects where a failed rollout went wrong, retains the prefix, injects an instruction as a new user turn, and regenerates the suffix. Costs are modest: training the small head requires failed-rollout data labeled only by final-answer correctness, and each correction consumes an additional partial regeneration, so inference budget grows with the number of interventions. It can fail when the MLP head's learned intervention points do not transfer to domains or reasoners unlike those in training, when the correctness signal is unavailable or noisy (limiting use outside verifiable tasks like math), and when extra regenerations erode the accuracy-per-compute advantage over simple majority voting. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Adaptive DHiSparse: Speculative Decoding over a Load-Adaptive KV Hierarchy
item.description: The method replaces fixed-budget hierarchical sparse KV serving (HiSparse) and non-speculative adaptive serving by combining host-memory KV offloading with exact fused retrieval, speculative decoding (DSpark/DFlash2), and residency that expands or contracts with load. It costs engineering complexity: shared missing-row retrieval across queries, a window-bounded draft KV ring, verification staging reused across layer groups, and a load-adaptive residency controller, plus host-memory capacity and PCIe transfer bandwidth. It can fail at low concurrency or short contexts where offload and retrieval overhead dominate, when host-GPU bandwidth is saturated, or if the exact retrieval path and speculative acceptance interact poorly with draft-model quality, eroding the acceptance-rate assumptions behind the throughput claims. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs
item.description: DUALQUANT replaces calibration-data-dependent activation quantization (e.g., SmoothQuant) and weight-only quantization with a calibration-free dual-scale method derived from weight-reconstruction MSE minimization, supporting MX and NVFP4 block formats. It costs the engineering effort of integrating a packed W4A4 kernel path and incurs some accuracy degradation relative to BF16, though the reported solver has closed-form updates and no calibration pipeline to maintain. It can fail on workloads whose accuracy tolerance is tighter than WikiText-2/C4 zero-shot benchmarks suggest, on models outside the evaluated Llama/Qwen families, and where native 4-bit hardware or mature W4A4 kernels are unavailable. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State
item.description: It replaces eager per-step SSM state reads/writes with a periodically updated checkpoint plus a buffer of recent SSM inputs, decoupling output computation from state updates and enabling cheap speculative rollback and split-precision checkpoints. The cost is additional implementation complexity in the serving stack (currently a vLLM patch for Mamba-2 and Gated DeltaNet), memory for the input buffer, and dual checkpoint copies when split precision is used. It can fail if checkpoint staleness degrades outputs for long unroll intervals, if the reader's model architecture lacks support in the implementation, or if batch sizes are too small for state I/O to be the bottleneck, in which case the measured gains do not transfer. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: test.

item.title: OccludeBench: Can VLMs Find What's Missing?
item.description: The technique replaces single-pass question answering about occluded objects with a two-step procedure in which the model first generates a candidate hidden object via inpainting and then evaluates that hypothesis against the visible physical cue. It costs an extra image-generation call and a second verification pass per query, and it is only available on models with image-generation capabilities; extended reasoning, tool use, and few-shot prompting were shown not to work reliably as alternatives. It can fail on the 50% of cases where models cannot recover the object from the projection in the full image, and the improvement is reported on only two models on a curated benchmark, so transfer to arbitrary production imagery is unverified. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems
item.description: FORTE replaces ad hoc or importance-score-based feature removal with a model-agnostic pipeline of efficient perturbation scoring, grouped ablation over candidate feature sets to capture interactions, lineage tracing of downstream consumer models, and offline-to-online validation before deprecation. Its cost is the engineering of daily perturbation evaluation, grouped retraining runs, lineage instrumentation, and A/B test capacity, which is substantial for a small team without existing experimentation infrastructure. It can fail when offline ablation results do not predict online behavior (the paper's own largest candidate set was rejected by online guardrails), when feature importance drifts faster than the evaluation cadence, or when coordinated deprecation across multiple consumer models stalls. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Returning to Development States: When Full Sandbox Snapshots Help Coding Agents
item.description: Replaces retry-from-scratch failure recovery in coding agents with Go-Explore-style branching from full environment snapshots (Daytona), preserving runtime state such as databases and services that a repository diff cannot reconstruct. Costs snapshot storage, snapshot/restore latency on each branch, added search and orchestration complexity, and dependency on an external sandbox provider. Can fail when progress lives only inside the repository (where a diff-based checkpoint suffices), when snapshots are large or slow to restore, or when restored runtime state diverges from a clean reproducible environment. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: test.

item.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
item.description: X-AgentRed replaces LLM-prompted or decomposition-based red-teaming, where harmful-path generation is biased toward familiar tool combinations, with a tool-dependency graph built from tool effects, preconditions, and harms, whose sampled paths are instantiated as scenarios and iteratively refined using execution feedback. The cost is a non-trivial implementation pipeline (tool-effect analysis, graph construction, scenario instantiation, and an execution-feedback loop) plus recurring LLM call costs for analysis and scenario generation, all feasible on API access without dedicated GPU hardware. It can fail where tool documentation is incomplete or inaccurate, since the dependency graph derives from inferred preconditions and effects, and discovered harms may not transfer across model versions, tool APIs, or permission configurations as services evolve. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Task-Sufficient Contraction: Source Selection for Machine Information Interfaces
item.description: The method replaces ad hoc task-agnostic compression or task-specific retraining of representations with a canonical reduced source, fixed before the encoder or rate is chosen, that merges states only when every action has identical regret, provably preserving the full rate-regret curve (and, for quadratic loss, reducing to projection onto directions in which feasible actions differ). It costs an information-theoretic analysis of the action set, loss, and feasible-action geometry per consumer task, plus a separate contraction per downstream task, and the paper offers theorems rather than implementations or benchmarks. It fails when the task's loss or action set is mis-specified, when merging is done too coarsely (the paper shows retaining only the optimal water-filled action loses information), or when approximate contractions are treated as exact. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: CARE: Certifying Acceleration for Vision-Language-Action Inference
item.description: CARE replaces ad hoc selection of VLA acceleration methods (action chunking, token pruning, flow-step reduction) based on latency and average success, instead running paired rollouts from identical initial conditions on a calibration set to certify that acceleration-induced failure risk stays below a user-specified budget, deploying the fastest certified candidate or falling back to the reference policy. The cost is calibration compute: paired closed-loop rollouts must be executed for each candidate, mitigated but not eliminated by sequential testing, and the method adds selection and fallback infrastructure around the serving stack. Certification guarantees are statistical and tied to the calibration distribution, so distribution shift between calibration and deployment initial conditions can invalidate the failure bound, and a tight risk budget may leave no certified accelerator, yielding no speedup at all. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SNR-Gated LSTM-Conditioned Diffusion Model for MIMO Channel Estimation
item.description: The method replaces per-snapshot least-squares and prior diffusion-based channel estimators for MIMO wireless systems with a temporally conditioned diffusion denoiser using an LSTM encoder, an SNR-gated fusion shortcut, and SNR-adaptive DDIM truncation. It costs the training of a domain-specific diffusion model on channel data, added inference complexity relative to classical estimators, and tuning of SNR-adaptive step schedules, with the abstract reporting no quantified improvement figures. It can fail under channel statistics or mobility patterns outside the training distribution, and its standardized-model simulations give no evidence of transfer to measured channels or to any task the reader operates. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: How Fragile Is On-Device Language Model Safety? Localizing Safety-Critical Parameters for Sparse Fault Analysis
item.description: The method replaces full-model safety auditing and uniform integrity protection with targeted analysis of a sparse safety-critical subset, mainly MLP down_proj weights localized via low-rank subspace analysis and parameter-level importance filtering. It costs the engineering effort of running the localization pipeline and adding selective integrity checks at deployment; the paper reports utility is preserved in the demonstrated attack case (51.6% vs 52.2% tinyBenchmarks accuracy). The approach can fail because localization is demonstrated only on LLaMA-2-7B-Chat and may not transfer to other SLM architectures, safety-critical parameters may shift under fine-tuning or quantization, and an attacker modifying weights outside the protected subset could still degrade safety. 0 independent implementations, 7 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SPIN: Shadow Predictive Indexer for Sparse Attention
item.description: SPIN replaces full KV-cache scoring by the sparse-attention indexer at every decoding step with lightweight history-based prediction of important KV blocks, integrated with speculative decoding. It requires adopting an indexer-based sparse attention stack and a vLLM implementation, adding prediction-model complexity and a modest integration cost rather than extra memory. It can fail when token-importance history is non-stationary, so workloads with abrupt topic shifts or long agentic trajectories may see quality degradation that the reported benchmarks do not cover. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Shared-Roadmap Generation and Evaluator for Multi-Agent Path Planning Using Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network
item.description: The method replaces hand-designed roadmap construction (lattice grids or standard sampling-based roadmaps) with a heterogeneous GNN that prunes redundant nodes and edges and ranks critical waypoints for multi-agent path planning. It costs a training pipeline dependent on occupation density maps aggregated from expert solver trajectories, plus graph construction and inference overhead at deployment. It can fail on environments or task distributions unlike the training data, since the learned pruning decisions inherit the expert solver's biases and the reported gains apply to dense-roadmap settings only. 2 independent implementations, 57 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: A Self-Pruning Transformer: Extreme KV-Cache Compression with Universal Attention
item.description: The method replaces RoPE positional embeddings with a composite trainable decay mechanism in a Universal Attention architecture, using the decay values as an adaptive criterion to prune low-contribution tokens from the KV cache during inference. The cost is that the mechanism is end-to-end trained, so it requires pretraining or fine-tuning the model itself rather than being a drop-in inference-time change to existing checkpoints, and it adds architectural complexity. It can fail if decay-based pruning degrades on workloads whose attention patterns differ from the evaluated natural language and synthetic tasks, if quality claims do not transfer to other model families, or if no pretrained checkpoints using this architecture become available for the reader's models. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Multi-Label Topic Assignment via LLM Distillation: A Comparative Analysis of Generative vs. Discriminative Student Models
item.description: The method replaces manual annotation with LLM-generated labels distilled into small student models, and replaces larger teacher inference at serving time with 1B-8B generative or discriminative classifiers. The cost is an offline teacher-labeling and distillation pipeline, plus the finding that the correct architecture is data-dependent: discriminative models win on structured reviews, generative models on conversational data, so a single architecture choice will not transfer across domains. It can fail if the LLM oracle's label errors propagate into the student, if the production taxonomy or label distribution drifts from the distilled training set, or if the reader's UGC is structured (where a cheaper discriminative baseline is sufficient) rather than conversational. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: TAP: Efficient Long-Horizon Agent Pruning via Trajectory-Anchored Recovery
item.description: TAP replaces one-shot importance-based pruning plus offline or full-trajectory distillation with iterative gradient-based channel re-scoring coupled to recovery, using a frozen dense teacher that anchors trajectories while the pruned student generates each response. It costs a pruning-and-recovery training pipeline: a frozen 7B teacher in memory, gradient computation for re-scoring, and RL-style trajectory rollouts, which is a substantial engineering and compute burden beyond simple post-hoc pruning. It can fail when applied to non-RL agents or tasks whose reward signals differ from ALFWorld/WebShop, and the WebShop retention of 88.0% shows meaningful task-dependent quality loss at 60% channel removal. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Tucker Bottleneck Attention for Multi-Dimensional Sequence Modeling
item.description: TuBA replaces full self-attention over long multidimensional token sequences (video frames, weather grids) with attention performed on compact low-rank Tucker cores, projecting hidden tensors down, mixing globally in the compressed space, and writing updates back. The cost is added architectural complexity: projection into and out of Tucker cores, a specialized autoregressive variant combining intra-core bidirectional and inter-core causal attention, and a rank hyperparameter that must be tuned per task. It can fail if the data lacks exploitable low-rank tensor structure, if the chosen core rank is too small and bottlenecks information flow, and its demonstrated gains are confined to video prediction and weather forecasting, with no evidence for language or general sequence workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MaRK: Markov-adapted Recurrent Kernels for Dynamic Operator Conditioning in State Space Models
item.description: MaRK replaces conventional input-injection or activation-modulation conditioning of pre-trained SSMs with low-rank auxiliary adapters (6.3-11M trainable parameters) that modulate a frozen backbone's recurrence, read-in, read-out, skip, and discretization operators directly. The cost is a custom adapter architecture tied to a specific 111M Hydra backbone and diffusion-style iterative generation, plus implementation complexity beyond standard LoRA-style fine-tuning. It can fail outside the demonstrated setting: results are limited to one backbone and validation loss comparisons across MaRK's own variants, with no evidence of transfer to other SSMs, tasks, or downstream quality metrics, and the stability certificate covers only the bounded modulated recurrence under the stated assumptions. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Q-PACE: Dynamic Precision Allocation for Quantization-Aware Training
item.description: Q-PACE replaces static or heuristic layer-precision assignments in mixed-precision quantization-aware training with a second-order sensitivity model that periodically recomputes per-layer curvature coefficients and reassigns precision under a memory budget. The cost is the added implementation complexity of curvature estimation and periodic perturbation-based recalibration during training, plus QAT's inherent training-time overhead relative to post-training quantization. It can fail if sensitivity estimates drift between recalibrations, if the second-order approximation misranks layers for architectures or tasks unlike those evaluated, or if the reader only performs inference-time quantization, in which case a training-time method offers no benefit. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Exact Dynamics and Finite-Sample Trajectory Recovery of Linear Recursive Feature Machines
item.description: Linear RFM replaces a trained neural network's representation-learning stage with an alternating loop of ridge-regularized linear fits and average-gradient-outer-product feature updates, all computable with closed-form linear algebra on CPU or a single small GPU. The cost is multiple full-data least-squares solves plus repeated d-by-d AGOP accumulations, which scales poorly with input dimension and sample count and provides only linear-model expressivity over learned features. It can fail when the low-rank teacher and isotropic sub-Gaussian input assumptions do not hold, and its real-data evidence is illustrative rather than benchmarked against tuned baselines. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Few Bits, One Law: Toward W2A4KV2
item.description: CanonQ replaces post-training quantization and per-tensor tuned QAT pipelines with a two-stage framework: fixed rotations and energy normalization map weights, activations, and KV caches into canonical coordinates so frozen Gaussian-reference codebooks can be shared, followed by joint quantization-aware training with an exact normalization-aware straight-through Jacobian. The cost is a full QAT stage, which requires training compute, backpropagation through the model, and implementation of the canonicalization and custom codebook interface rather than a simple calibration pass, making 8B-scale application difficult on a single 24 GB GPU. It can fail if the frozen-codebook transfer assumption breaks on out-of-distribution models or tasks, if rotation/normalization overhead adds inference latency without a compatible kernel implementation, or if the claimed gains do not replicate on the reader's specific model and serving stack. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CurveTQ: Rotation-Free Trellis Quantization of LLM Weights via Curvature-Weighted Search
item.description: CurveTQ replaces the random orthogonal rotation used by state-of-the-art 2-bit trellis quantizers (QTIP, Proteus) with a curvature-weighted Viterbi branch metric in the native basis, plus a start state per coding block that alone lifts baselines by 1-3 points. It costs no runtime rotation to undo during decoding, making inference faster, but requires implementing or adopting a new codec with a factored scale field, quantile table, and per-block state storage. It can fail if the accuracy claims do not transfer beyond the three 4-8B models and one 35B MoE tested, if the implementation is not yet mature or integrated with the reader's inference stack, or if the small residual gap to full rotation-based methods matters for a specific workload. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Quantize by Drift: Label-Free Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization for Text Embedders
item.description: The method replaces relevance-label-based or search-based per-module sensitivity estimation for mixed-precision post-training quantization of text embedders with a label-free signal: quantize one module, re-encode the corpus, and measure how far output embeddings drift, then allocate precision additively under a packed-byte budget. It costs one quantization pass per module plus a full corpus re-encoding per measurement, with no labels, no search, and only modest engineering complexity. It can fail as an allocation objective: at the main budget it underperformed same-budget uniform precision on all three sealed embedders, so it is justified mainly at stressed budgets where uniform precision collapses, and fine-grained redistribution around a strong uniform operating point remains unresolved. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: An Interleaved Parallel Dependent Quantization Hardware Architecture for H.266/VVC
item.description: The architecture replaces the serial dependent quantization stage in H.266/VVC encoders with a four-channel interleaved parallel design using time-division multiplexed combinational logic, intra-CG context simplification, and skipped decAbslevel rate estimation. The cost is a small compression penalty (0.38-0.42% BDBR) plus the need for FPGA or ASIC implementation in Verilog, which is far outside software-only ML infrastructure. Adoption risk is irrelevant for an ML engineer, but in its own domain the simplifications could interact poorly with encoder configurations or content classes not covered by the reported test conditions. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: SearchWorld: Spatial Value-Grounded Imagination for UAV Object Search via World Models
item.description: Replaces reactive explicit-map search policies with a recurrent state-space world model that decodes a task-aware spatial value layer from BEV exploration and obstacle memory, enabling planning via imagined rollouts without a separate scalar critic. Costs include a staged training pipeline (world-model learning, expert imitation, imagination refinement), a simulation environment, and added inference compute for rollouts, though it avoids image-generating world-model latency. It can fail because absolute success remains low (23.8%), the approach is validated only on one UAV benchmark, and transfer to real flight demands sim-to-real adaptation beyond an ML engineer's typical scope. 0 independent implementations, 216 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Shared Low-rank Basis Factorization for Data-free Mixture-of-Experts Compression
item.description: Replaces expert pruning and expert merging for reducing MoE model size, instead reconstructing each expert's weights from a rank-k basis shared across experts, plus a post-hoc gauge fixing step that removes redundant parameters. It is data-free, so it avoids calibration data and retraining, but it costs a reconstruction pass over the full model and adds factorization/gauge-fixing implementation complexity; the compressed model also requires kernels or formats that exploit the low-rank shared structure to realize storage or serving gains. It can fail if the chosen rank is too low for heterogeneous experts, if reconstruction error compounds in downstream task accuracy, or if the reader's serving stack cannot exploit the factored weights, and applying it to 16B–122B models requires memory headroom beyond a single 24 GB GPU during compression. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: OnlineQAT: On-Policy Distillation for Ultra-Low-Bit Large Language Models
item.description: OnlineQAT replaces offline quantization-aware training on fixed or teacher-generated completions with a two-stage pipeline: block-wise QAT initialization followed by on-policy distillation, where a frozen full-precision teacher supplies a sampled reverse-KL signal at prefixes the quantized student itself generates. The cost is a full training recovery stage rather than post-training quantization: the teacher must be served during training, the student must generate responses on-policy (adding sampling latency per step), and one 24 GB GPU constrains this to small models such as 1.7B-scale with offloading or gradient checkpointing. It can fail if the workload cannot absorb training cost (a static PTQ method may be preferable), the marginal W2A16 gain of 0.44 points may not transfer to other models or tasks, and student sampling introduces variance and hyperparameter sensitivity absent from fixed-completion training. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MemoWM: How World Models Change What Agents Need to Remember
item.description: It replaces storing complete per-experience records in agent memory with a task-aware allocation rule that retains only information whose downstream value exceeds what a shared world model can predict and reconstruct. The cost is maintaining and querying a world model (parameter storage and inference overhead per memory write/read) plus an allocation scoring step, and total storage only improves if the world-model capacity stays below the recurring storage it saves. It can fail when the world model mispredicts task-relevant content, causing reconstruction errors on omitted details; quality therefore degrades on workloads whose regularities the world model has not captured. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Plan-and-Patch: Diffusion Language Models for Agentic Planning
item.description: The method replaces full autoregressive plan regeneration, in which a failed step forces the entire plan to be rewritten, with a diffusion language model that regenerates only the masked, invalidated region while holding the surrounding plan steps fixed. The cost is adopting a non-standard diffusion LLM stack (e.g., DreamReasoner-8B) with its parallel-unmasking inference path, plus implementing plan parsing and region-selection logic to identify what to patch. Failure modes include incorrect localization of the region needing repair, degradation when a failure invalidates most of the plan rather than a contiguous segment, and dependence on a dLLM ecosystem that is less mature and less supported than AR serving infrastructure. 2 independent implementations, 136 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: test.

item.title: On the Clock: Towards Punctual and Productive Time-Budgeted AI Agents
item.description: The approach replaces unstated or prompt-only time budgets with harness-exposed timing signals, optional deadline-enforcement hooks, and optionally GRPO training with budget-aware rewards. The harness mechanisms cost little (minor instrumentation and prompt tokens for timing feedback), while the RL variant adds training compute and reward-engineering complexity. It can fail to convert adherence into productivity: agents that respect the budget still fill extra time with repeated actions, and multi-budget GRPO training tends to collapse toward the shortest-budget strategy. 2 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: RFChipAgent: Multi-Agentic AI Flow for Analog/RF Chip Design
item.description: The method replaces manual analog/RF circuit design steps (topology selection, schematic and testbench assembly, circuit sizing) with a multi-agent LLM pipeline combining multimodal RAG over engineering documents, a hybrid TPE/CMA-ES sizing optimizer, and a simulator-in-the-loop evaluation with a trust-scored results database. Adoption costs include access to a commercial process design kit (GF22FDSOI), circuit simulators, per-document FAISS infrastructure, and sustained LLM API usage, none of which serve an ML inference or training workload. It can fail through incorrect topology or schematic generation requiring expert human supervision, and its validation is limited to a single 60 GHz LNA family, so generality across circuits and processes is unestablished. 1 independent implementation, 14 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Reading the Room: Foundations, Design, and Challenges of Normative Competence in LLMs
item.description: The work introduces a synthetic multi-agent debate benchmark that replaces informal assumptions that LLMs can infer community norms from interaction, and it is a diagnostic evaluation rather than a deployable technique. It costs nothing to adopt in production but reproducing it requires building a custom multi-agent simulation harness, and the tested normative modules add architectural complexity without reliable gains. Its central finding is a failure mode: agents copy idiosyncratic noise alongside enforced norms and norm-following is highly sensitive to norm style and module backbone, so any deployment relying on interaction-inferred behavioral rules can silently mimic spurious behavior. 1 independent implementation, 126 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: StoreBench: A Live-Commerce Environment for Evaluating and Training Autonomous Operator Agents
item.description: StoreBench replaces static agentic benchmarks with a deterministic, live-commerce RL environment using 29 merchant tools, calibrated pass thresholds, and reward-hack hardening for evaluation and GRPO post-training. It costs engineering effort to stand up a production-grade commerce backend and run multi-day simulated episodes, and the full environment and evaluation suite are withheld, so independent adoption requires reimplementing or waiting for release. It can fail because gains from training on five tasks may not transfer beyond this narrow commerce domain, the released artifacts cover only a fraction of the benchmark, and heuristic-calibrated thresholds may not reflect real business value. 2 independent implementations, 136 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Cross-Provider Review as a Runtime Contract for Coding Agents: A Controlled Pilot and Fault-Injection Study
item.description: The method replaces informal or absent second-opinion review of coding-agent output with a structured advisory contract spanning distinct provider resource pools, bounded execution, restricted reviewer capabilities, complete input delivery, and durable per-attempt evidence. It costs an additional API call from a separate subscription pool per reviewed turn, plus implementation and maintenance of the contract machinery; the pilot found substantive findings in only 8 of 20 paired turns, and some review calls yielded nothing useful. Fault injection exposed real failure modes: false success on truncated input, cancellation during process reaping, and a nonzero-exit reviewer with a well-formed verdict being counted as complete, the last of which invalidated the accrued 25-observation shadow-study cohort. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Curating Always-Loaded Context for LLM Agents: A Capacitated Assortment Model with Censored Feedback
item.description: Replaces append-only growth of always-loaded context files (AGENTS.md and equivalents) with a capacitated selection procedure that keeps only a bounded subset of instructions under a token budget. Costs curator effort or an automated selection loop, instrumentation of per-instruction compliance, and accepts the formal result that removing apparently ignored instructions can inevitably delete helpful ones because feedback on loaded items is observable while absent items are censored. Can fail when compliance attribution to individual instructions is noisy, when token price is misestimated, or when reviewer throughput limits how many add/remove edits can be validated per period. 1 independent implementation, 14 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Prompts versus Rules: Auditing and Controlling Speech Naturalness Behaviors in Voice User Simulators
item.description: The method replaces prompt-only control of disfluency, interruption, and backchanneling in LLM-based voice user simulators with a deterministic, model-free injection algorithm, plus an audit of realized rather than configured behaviors. It costs little in compute or infrastructure since it is rule-based, but adds implementation and validation effort for the injection logic and the auditing pipeline. It can fail if the rules encode unnatural placement or distributions for a given language or domain, and its advantage over prompting was shown only on the authors' tau-Voice setup across three models, so transferability to other simulators is unverified. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: NOMOS: Compiling Written Policies into Statically Verified Tool-Call Gates for LLM Agents
item.description: Replaces hand-written guard rules and per-action LLM verifiers with a four-pass compiler that turns natural-language policy into a deterministic, statically verified tool-call gate, compilable on-premise with an open-weight 26B model. Costs are a one-time compilation pipeline, a transcript-replay validation step, and a domain-dependent benign-utility cost from over-refusal, since a bad binding was observed refusing 95.9% of legitimate task-passing calls. Can fail on attack goals that involve no governable tool call, on bindings verified as weaker than their clause, and in domains where policy clauses cannot be grounded in available tool schemas. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AgentHorizon: Evaluating Agentic Judges for Long-Horizon Computer-Use Tasks
item.description: The benchmark replaces ad hoc or human-only inspection of computer-use agent trajectories with a paired instruction-swap evaluation that measures whether automatic judges can distinguish a successful trajectory from a similar but incompatible one. Adopting it costs API spend or GPU inference to run judges over trajectories of up to 300 screenshots, plus engineering effort to integrate either direct trajectory passing or agent-harness-based judging into the evaluation pipeline. The main failure modes are that even the best judge reaches only 80.9% balanced accuracy, that tool-use degrades open-weight judge performance, and that individual judges show strong asymmetric biases toward accepting valid or rejecting failed trajectories, so a single judge should not be trusted as an unsupervised success signal. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: When Interfaces Speak: Data-Aware Generative UI Harness for Active Interaction
item.description: The method replaces purely text-based agent interaction with a two-agent harness in which a Tool Agent retrieves and executes while a GUI Coder Agent generates task-specific front-end code, optionally trained with RL using sandbox-collected rewards audited by a meta-reward mechanism. Costs include building and maintaining the Dynamic UX sandbox for reward collection, RL training of a small backbone, the Reward Auditor's additional inference overhead, and front-end rendering latency in the interaction loop. The reported gains are measured on a new benchmark built from ten domain databases, so transfer to other workloads is unverified, and LLM-as-a-Judge reward hacking is mitigated rather than eliminated, meaning rubric drift or auditor failure could silently degrade training. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Do LLMs Learn from Rewards in Context? : Rethinking the role of reward in In-Context Reinforcement Learning
item.description: The paper evaluates, rather than proposes, a technique: it tests whether appending raw trajectory-reward pairs to an LLM's context functions as inference-time RL, and finds it does not; reward signals are read but flipping, randomizing, or removing them leaves improvement curves nearly unchanged, and even corrupted trajectories help as much as real ones. It replaces nothing directly, but its finding implies that engineering effort spent on reward shaping, reward-aware prompting, and exploration instructions for context-based agent memory is largely wasted, and should instead go toward input distribution and demonstration quality as in standard ICL. The cost of acting on this finding is low, but it can fail to transfer: the experiments cover four benchmarks and six models in the direct ICRL setting, so results may not hold for structured memory architectures, larger models, or domains where reward semantics are genuinely informative. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Skill Constellations: Tracing the Supply Chain of Agent Skills on GitHub
item.description: This is an empirical supply-chain measurement of SKILL.md files on GitHub plus a ranking model that prioritizes which source repositories to audit, replacing the common heuristic of using GitHub stars to identify influential skill sources. It costs nothing to adopt directly as an inference technique because it is a dataset and analysis, but reproducing it requires processing git history across 2.19 million skill adoptions, which exceeds a constrained team's practical scope; the usable artifact is the released viewer and ranked list. It can fail if copy patterns shift after the study's snapshot, if private or non-GitHub skill distribution dominates an organization's exposure, or if 'high-risk' labels in the dataset do not match the adopter's threat model. 2 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: VAMR: Multi-Question Agentic Reasoning for Efficient Long-Form Video Understanding
item.description: VAMR replaces isolated per-question tool-use trajectories for long-form video understanding with one shared trajectory that jointly gathers evidence and maintains layered multi-question memory, trained via SFT plus question-horizon policy optimization. The cost is a training pipeline (supervised fine-tuning plus RL with a question-level critic) and a more complex orchestration and memory design, which exceeds a simple API-call setup unless a pretrained checkpoint is available. It can fail when one difficult question extends the shared trajectory for all questions, when errors in the shared video story propagate across answers, and when the trained policy does not transfer to video domains or tools outside its training distribution. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Who Pays the Review Cost? Triage, Fairness, and Accountability in AI-authored Pull Requests
item.description: Replaces ad hoc or categorical acceptance of AI-generated pull requests with an intake policy requiring bounded scope, project-grounded rationale, validation beyond CI, contributor responsiveness, and identifiable post-merge ownership before consuming reviewer time. Costs are process overhead: authors of agent-generated code must supply rationale, validation evidence, and ownership commitments, adding friction to submission pipelines without additional compute. It can fail when human stewardship is not genuinely observable, when validation claims are superficial or unverifiable, or when teams lack reviewer capacity to enforce the gate, in which case reviewability debt accumulates silently. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: What to Admit and How to Present: Governing Persistent Memory in LLM Agents
item.description: The method replaces verbatim injection (or relevance-only selection) of persistent memory entries with inference-time admission policies that adjudicate entries or typed sub-units against deterministic eligibility rules before they enter the working context. It costs additional adjudication calls and policy engineering per memory write/read, adding latency and implementation complexity, with no retraining required. It can fail by increasing personalization failures—both designs did—and PS missed its preregistered improvement and personalization-preservation criteria, so beneficial memory use may be lost while safety improves. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SafeInferCom: Safe Inference-Time Compute via Verifier-Guided Mid-Generation Intervention for Robotic Task Planning
item.description: SafeInferCom replaces one-shot or iteratively refined reasoning for robotic task planning with an inference-time monitor that exposes and verifies intermediate plans, preserving valid ones and directing correction without restarting decoding. It costs an additional formal verifier per planning domain, monitoring overhead during generation, and integration complexity with the decoding loop; the abstract claims reduced token usage versus refinement alone but gives no figures. It can fail where no formal verifier exists for the target domain, where verification itself is imperfect, or where the reader's workload is standard text generation rather than constraint-driven robotic planning. 1 independent implementation, 4 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: REMORY: Learning Residual Memory for Context Compaction
item.description: REMORY replaces the plain-text summary used in context compaction with a summary plus a bounded sequence of learned soft memory tokens, appended as a residual along the sequence dimension to recover information the summary dropped. The cost is training a separate memory network per backbone LLM against a frozen model's continuation objective, plus the inference-time overhead of generating the tokens, which demands gradient-level access to the target model during training and is impractical for API-only or 27B-class models on a single 24 GB GPU. It can fail when deployed on a backbone or domain different from the training setup, since the soft tokens are model-specific and their benefit is validated mainly on summarization-attribution and two agent benchmarks rather than general workloads. 3 independent implementations, 169 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: DuplexAgent-RSI: Recursive Harness Improvement for Full-Duplex Voice Agent Collaboration
item.description: The method replaces hand-tuned, coupled heuristics for coordinating a full-duplex voice model with asynchronous reasoning/coding delegates by a six-module editable harness plus a closed loop (simulator, exam planner, harness editor) that revises those modules from interaction traces. Adoption costs substantial engineering: a full-duplex interaction model, a delegation pool of reasoning LLMs and coding agents, a conversation simulator, and the diagnosis/repair infrastructure, with added per-interaction latency and API spend from the improvement loop. Failure modes include the repair loop overfitting to simulator-generated conversations that misrepresent real users, incorrect failure attribution across the six modules, and regressions from automated module edits reaching production without adequate verification. 1 independent implementation, 14 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Democratizing MoE inference on commodity GPUs with CoMoE
item.description: CoMoE replaces inter-GPU P2P token routing and global-synchronization combine in expert parallelism with host-mediated multicast dispatch and fine-grained token-level aggregation via host staging buffers. The cost is added host-memory staging, host-bandwidth dependency, and engineering complexity, and the gains are demonstrated only on multi-GPU RTX 5090 setups, which exceed the reader's single 24 GB GPU. It can fail if host PCIe bandwidth or CPU memory becomes the new bottleneck, if workloads do not exhibit the token-sharing patterns the multicast exploits, or if straggler mitigation benefits do not materialize on different model and batch configurations. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: DSReg: Provably Recovering Individual World Latents without Reconstruction
item.description: DSReg replaces reconstruction-based or supervision-based disentanglement methods (nonlinear ICA, dictionary learning, causal representation learning with decoders or labels) with a post hoc regularization applied to any linearly identified representation, such as LeJEPA checkpoints. Its cost is low: no decoder, no labels, no retraining of the base model, and reuse of existing checkpoints at no loss versus joint training, which fits a single-GPU budget. It can fail if the Structural Diversity assumption does not hold, i.e., when two latents leave sufficiently similar dependency footprints on observations, since identifiability then degrades and no reconstruction signal exists to correct the mixing. 1 independent implementation, 228 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CHASE: Channel-Aligned Structure Exploitation for Geometry-Aware Model Engineering
item.description: CHASE replaces heuristic MHA-to-GQA conversion, layer-wise KV-cache allocation, and uniform structured pruning with geometry-driven choices: CAGA constructs shared KV heads by geometric alignment and low-rank subspace extraction, SAKV selects which adjacent layers share a low-rank KV representation and their ranks, and CAPS selects retained input channels per output-neuron group. The cost is one-off SVD/spectral analysis of trained weights plus implementation complexity across three separate method variants, with no stated inference-time overhead beyond the compressed artifacts. Failure modes include misalignment when weight spectra do not exhibit the assumed concentration, quality loss from incorrect shared-head or layer-group assignment on out-of-distribution workloads, and unverifiable benefit here because the abstract reports only qualitative superiority over baselines without numbers. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Physics-Informed Neural Plasticity: PDE Solvers That Reshape Themselves
